title: The Vanishing Data
briefing_md:
ShopSphere is a fictional online marketplace for small sellers.

On Wednesday 22 October at 7:15 AM, customers opening the app saw "You have no orders". Sellers' dashboards were empty too. 3,412 order records from the last 30 days are missing from the production orders table. Nobody on the day team deleted anything.

The company's senior DBA, Neha, resigned two weeks ago and was working late on Tuesday night. People are already pointing fingers.

Find out where the orders went, who or what is responsible, and how to get them back and stop it happening again.
root_cause_options: Human error during an approved change
Bad or wrongly formatted input data
Test or staging activity hitting production
twist_md: Two more records have been pulled: the code change (PR #812) behind Tuesday's deployment, and the complete database audit of Neha's Tuesday-night session.

answer.root_cause_md: Before the twist, the departing DBA's late-night session, bulk export, resignation email and the AI analysis all point at an insider. Careful teams notice the deletion was run by svc_archiver with interval '0 days' (E02, E09), the config reads ARCHIVER_RETENTION_DAYS with default 0 while production only sets RETENTION_DAYS (E07, E08), and Neha's role cannot delete (E16).
answer.post_twist_responsible: archiver v2.0.0 (PR #812) renamed the retention setting to ARCHIVER_RETENTION_DAYS with a default of 0; production still set RETENTION_DAYS=30, so the 03:00 run archived and deleted every order. The data is safe in s3://shopsphere-archive/orders/archive_2026-10-22.parquet and can be restored.
